items.followUp: A machine receives 500 J of energy and produces 350 J of useful work. Calculate its efficiency.

rubric.why: Checks that efficiency is defined as the ratio of useful output to total input.
rubric.description: Defines efficiency as useful output work or energy divided by total input work or energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying both the useful output and total input in the correct ratio.

rubric.why: Checks the mathematical formula for percentage efficiency.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula, including multiplication by 100 for percentage efficiency.

modelAnswer: Efficiency is the ratio of useful output work (or energy) to total input work (or energy).

items.followUp: A motor produces 45 J of useful work from 300 J of input energy. Find its efficiency.

rubric.why: Checks the correct substitution of useful work and input energy into the efficiency ratio.
rubric.description: Substitutes 12 J of useful work and 100 J of input energy into the efficiency formula.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct ratio, 12 J ÷ 100 J.
Award 1 mark for the correct answer with the percent unit.

modelAnswer: Given: useful work = 12 J; input energy = 100 J.

items.followUp: State Newton’s second law of motion and use it to obtain F = ma for a body of constant mass.

rubric.why: Checks the main statement of Newton’s second law.
rubric.description: States that the rate of change of momentum is directly proportional to the applied force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the proportionality statement.

rubric.why: Checks the direction specified by the law.
rubric.description: States that the change in momentum takes place in the direction of the force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct direction.

rubric.why: Checks the momentum relation used in the explanation.
rubric.description: Uses momentum p = mv for a body of constant mass.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct momentum expression.

rubric.why: Checks the final mathematical form for constant mass.
rubric.description: Obtains Newton’s second-law equation F = ma.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct final equation.

modelAnswer: Newton’s second law states that the rate of change of momentum of a body is directly proportional to the applied force and takes place in the direction of that force.
For a body of constant mass, rate of change of momentum = (mv − mu) ÷ t = m(v − u) ÷ t = ma.
Therefore, F ∝ ma; in SI units, F = ma.

items.followUp: A vehicle starts from rest and travels 600 m in 60 s with uniform acceleration. Find its speed at the end of 60 s.

rubric.why: Checks the given quantities, including conversion of the distance to SI units.
rubric.description: Identifies u = 0, s = 1000 m, and t = 100 s.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly recording the initial speed, distance, and time.

rubric.why: Checks the appropriate equation and its substitution.
rubric.description: Uses s = ut + ½at² and substitutes the known values.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct equation with a valid substitution.

rubric.why: Checks the acceleration calculated from the distance and time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct acceleration with unit.

rubric.why: Checks the method used to calculate the final speed.
rubric.description: Uses v = u + at and substitutes the initial speed, acceleration, and time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct final-velocity equation and substitution.

rubric.why: Checks the final speed and its unit.
rubric.description: Obtains a final speed of 20 m/s.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct answer with unit.

modelAnswer: Given: u = 0 m/s, s = 1 km = 1000 m, t = 100 s.
Using v = u + at: v = 0 m/s + (0.2 m/s²)(100 s).
The speed at the end of 100 s is 20 m/s.
